<reason>Both sides argued well, but B's core mechanism — employer coverage withdraws the policy at the moment the claim arrives — survived the whole exchange. A conceded the design flaw immediately and staked the case on (1) existing patches, (2) monopoly lock/Canada's ban on duplicate cover, and (3) Vermont/Colorado as cost evidence. B damaged all three. On patches, B's pressure question ("name a real exit for the 55-year-old with cancer") forced A to answer "her exit is subsidized exchange coverage," which B converted into the debate's cleanest frame: every door A offers opens into public financing, so the real dispute is floor versus trapdoor, and doors only help the healthy and employed. A's reply that a plural net is not an argument for one payer was genuinely good and kept the comparison live, but it never fully answered the late/means-tested/mid-treatment-network harms. On Canada, B correctly narrowed the ban to duplicate cover of insured services and tied the queue to capacity and funding choices, and A partly conceded ("the ban is a choice — but a structural one"), which softened A's earlier claim that floor-plus-layers is "fictional" — especially damaging since the motion is confined to *basic* coverage. On Vermont, B's ERISA/federal-tax-subsidy/state-line explanation plus the Medicare popularity contrast largely converted A's evidence into a passability point, and A's fallback ("relabeling, not saving") does not defeat B's coverage-security harm. A's single-point-of-failure weighing stayed abstract, and its NHS "third rail" line arguably cut against its own underfunding story. B's rebuttal 2 being clipped is a real execution cost, and A's closing was efficient and pointed, which keeps this competitive rather than lopsided.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Pressure Q1 demanding a real exit for the sick 55-year-old, and A's answer conceding that the exit is subsidized exchange coverage — which B then crystallized as "every door CON offers opens into the same room: public financing," reframing the clash as floor versus trapdoor rather than one payer versus many.</best_rebuttal>
